overview: Client library holds the hash ring (150 virtual nodes per server) from service discovery and talks to nodes directly. Each key is replicated to the next node on the ring.

estimation.assumption: Illustrative hot set: 10M keys at 1 KB/value.
estimation.calculation: 10,000,000 × 1 KB ≈ 10 GB payload; two copies ≈ 20 GB before overhead.
estimation.result: Metadata, fragmentation and failover headroom increase the memory budget.
estimation.implication: Partition memory across shards; size for a failed shard moving to survivors.

components.rationale: Health checks and routing policy support scale-out; connection-based systems need compatible session routing.

components.purpose: Smart client library holds the consistent hashing ring (150 virtual nodes per server); local near cache for hot keys
components.rationale: Keep request handlers stateless where possible; the datastore or a fenced owner enforces concurrency invariants.

components.purpose: Each key also written to the next node on the ring (replica) for failover
components.rationale: Specify TTL and update strategy; durable state remains elsewhere unless an atomic admission decision explicitly depends on this store.

components.purpose: Gossip heartbeats; publishes the ring to clients
components.rationale: Refresh stale metadata and bound retries; avoid treating an old map as permanent ownership.

components.purpose: Store authoritative records with transactional constraints for distributed cache.
components.rationale: Choose keys and indexes from the documented access patterns; replicas provide availability, not conflict-free arbitrary writes.

entityDetails.purpose: Disposable hot data with bounded staleness.
accessPatterns: GET by key; SET/DELETE by key; bulk warmup only with rate limits.
constraints: TTL and eviction can remove any entry. Cache failure must not become permanent data loss.

apiDetails.purpose: Read a key from its owning cache shard.
apiDetails.rationale: Client-ring or proxy routing chooses the shard. A miss causes the application, not the cache, to fetch the source of truth.
Hash key routing must be consistent for GET and SET. Never treat replication of cached data as a durable write guarantee.

steps.title: Users → LB → App servers
steps.explanation: The application owns validation and the source-of-truth fallback.

steps.title: App servers → Membership
steps.explanation: Refresh the versioned consistent-hash ring when membership changes.

steps.title: App servers → Cache cluster
steps.explanation: Hash the key to its cache shard; return the value if present and unexpired.

steps.title: App servers → Cache cluster
steps.explanation: A missing or expired key returns MISS, not an application failure.

steps.title: App servers → Source of truth
steps.explanation: Fetch the authoritative record with request coalescing.

steps.title: App servers → Cache cluster
steps.explanation: Populate the disposable entry with a jittered TTL and return the durable value.

failureCases.scenario: A cache shard dies or membership changes
failureCases.handling: Treat misses as recoverable; rebuild gradually with request coalescing and jittered TTLs. Bound source-of-truth load, and version membership to prevent inconsistent routing loops.

alternatives: Use a client-side ring when applications can share a versioned routing library. Use proxies/hash slots for simpler clients, accepting another hop and a separately scaled routing fleet.
